census: local-lane session inheritance by the run's own session join
after_window_rule: local dispatch run-id timestamp > 2026-09-23T10:40:20Z, the committer time of adbb606797e2561dcc31758e49458f1d1bac3fef, which keyed session reuse to the run's own task

parser.resume_recovered_from: the session id in the run's own opening stream record: a run that inherits an earlier transcript opens the same session, a fresh run opens a new one, so sharing an id is the only durable record of what the first turn actually sent
parser.session_join: run dirs are grouped by the session id their own stream opens with, ordered by run-id timestamp; the earlier run is recorded as the one that built the history
parser.first_request_input: the first assistant record's message.usage charged input (input_tokens plus the disjoint cache read/create fields where published)
parser.cumulative_input: not read on this lane: the terminal result record carries it, and this scan reads only a bounded prefix ending at the first assistant turn
parser.task_worktree: the cwd recorded in the run's own opening record, which names the worktree the run worked in
parser.task_identity: the identity the session-reuse rule keys on: (project, plan, node) for an implement, test or investigate run, and the reviewed node for a review; the reviewed node's name is a simplification of the dispatch rule's reviewed-run id, held here so this file compares with the codex census field for field
parser.runs_in_session: the local grammar publishes no rollout, so the count the codex census records as tasks_in_rollout is here the number of local run directories sharing the session
parser.read_bound: each stream is read only until its first charged assistant turn, never past 20000 lines or 67108864 bytes
parser.lane_rule: a run is on the local lane when its recorded backend is local — the run store's backend for the run, or the run directory's launch record where the store holds no row, local backends being ('clive', 'clive-glm') — and its own stream opens the claude grammar, which is the grammar this lane runs and the only one that publishes a first-turn figure; runs recorded local whose stream opens the codex grammar are counted separately and excluded, because their stream is another attempt's
parser.launch_record_coverage: the run directory's launch records (attempt.json, worker.json) begin on 2026-09-24, so a resume declared in argv is measurable for the after window only; the before window's declared resumes are unrecorded rather than zero
parser.same_task_resumes: an inherited transcript whose task identity matches this run's, including a run that continues its own session
parser.cross_task_resumes: an inherited transcript whose task identity differs from this run's: the condition the reuse rule removes

declared_resumes.rule: a launch record whose argv carries --resume <session> is a dispatch asking to continue that session; its owner is the latest local run before it whose own stream opened the same session, and a declaration whose owner is not in the population is recorded unresolved rather than guessed; where a run holds several attempt records, the latest declaring attempt is the one counted

statement: cross-task resumes are zero over 1439 local-lane dispatches after 2026-09-23T10:40:20Z; same-task resumes number 0; 148 dispatches declare a resume in a launch record, of which 148 target their own task, 0 another task and 0 an owner outside the population
scan_notes: The first-record histogram is the scan's own positive control: the claude dialect (3695 runs) and the codex dialect (3017 runs) are both present, so the scan discriminates rather than returning nothing.
rows_note: Per-run rows are stored for every resume in both windows and for the most recent 25 fresh runs per window; the window summaries count every dispatch.
reuse_window_note: Every local dispatch after the boundary opened a new session in its own stream, so the stream population alone would read as a window in which no session was reused at all. Reuse was still exercised: 148 dispatches carry a launch record declaring a resume, of which 148 target the declaring run's own task, 0 another task and 0 an owner outside the population. The cross-task zero is therefore read over a window in which the reuse path was taken, and the declarations are attributed by the same identity the stream classification uses.
